title: Windowed `SUM`/`AVG` of doubles: a segment tree of fanout 16, or per-thread partials
verdict: a tree of sequential nodes (fanout 16) for framed windows; per-thread sequential partials for a whole-partition frame
description: A windowed `sum` or `avg` of doubles picks its aggregator in order: DISTINCT a merge sort tree; a frame that is the whole partition (`OVER ()`, or unbounded on both sides, or `CURRENT ROW` in RANGE mode without ORDER BY) `WindowConstantAggregator`; otherwise `WindowSegmentTree` (`sum` has no custom window callback). The constant aggregator adds each thread's rows of a partition in turn to a local state and combines the local states into the partition's state. The segment tree sums each run of 16 rows in turn into a leaf state, and each level combines 16 states of the level below in turn; a frame's state takes the ragged leaf values on its left, then whole nodes level by level, then the ragged right parts, each added in turn. All of it is the aggregate's `+=` and combine (duckdb-sum-double), in `DOUBLE`.

Order class: (a) a tree whose nodes add their children in turn: fanout 16 for framed windows, with the frame's own node adding up to 15 leaf values and 30 nodes per level; per-thread sequential partials combined in finishing order for whole-partition frames. (b) Any tree: |ŝ − s| ≤ γ_h Σ|x_i| with h the most additions on one value's path (Higham §4.2); h ≤ n − 1 always, and for a framed window of n rows h grows with 45·⌈log₁₆ n⌉ (15 in each node on the way up, up to 30 in the frame's node per level), an estimate from the code's shape. `avg` divides once more. Within #85's bounds. (c) The source below; a probe at one thread gives 0.9999999999999999 for a running sum and an `OVER ()` sum of ten 0.1, the same as adding them in turn. (d) ANY (`FloatSums`): a framed window's sum is a tree sum of the frame's values, which SEQUENTIAL does not cover for frames over 16 rows. A whole-partition frame at one thread is SEQUENTIAL.
The docs are silent on the summation order of windowed aggregates: a docs gap. No upstream test pins the double rounding; it may change between versions.
reference: `sum_order` over the frame: any order and grouping within #85's bound (`FloatSums`), as for `SUM` of doubles.

evidence.note: aggregator choice: distinct, constant, custom, segment tree, naive
Finalize: local state combined into the global one
EvaluateUpperLevels: left parts, whole nodes, right parts in order
Higham, Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms (2nd ed., SIAM 2002), ch. 4 Summation: §4.2 recursive, pairwise and any-order bounds; §4.3 compensated summation

evidence.sql: SET threads = 1; SELECT sum(v) OVER (ORDER BY i ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)::VARCHAR FROM (SELECT 0.1::DOUBLE v, i FROM range(10) r(i)) QUALIFY i = 9; SELECT sum(v) OVER ()::VARCHAR FROM (SELECT 0.1::DOUBLE v, i FROM range(10) r(i)) LIMIT 1

provenance.notes: DuckDB 2.0.0 (Python, macOS arm64), a scratch script. Ten rows fit one leaf, so this shows the sequential leaf; a frame over more than 16 rows that tells the tree from the sequential sum is still to probe.
